parts.title: Part A — Short messages
parts.instructions: Listen and choose the correct answer.

items.prompt: When is the delegation expected to arrive?

parts.title: Part B — Short conversations
parts.instructions: Listen to each conversation and choose the correct answer.

items.prompt: What does the client conclude?

competence.raw: M-I · 1.4 · tecnicismos + modales en pasiva · listening

options.text: they cannot rebook until the account is cleared
the fee has already been paid

audio.transcript: — Under GDS rules, your cancellation fee might be waived, but the account is currently flagged for compliance review. — Meaning that we cannot rebook until it is cleared?

items.prompt: What is the investor confirming through paraphrase?

competence.raw: M-I · 1.5 · paráfrasis avanzada / confirmar comprensión · listening

options.text: that the commission would be reinvested locally

audio.transcript: — So, if I understand you correctly, you mean that the commission would be reinvested locally? — Precisely. That is exactly what I mean.

items.prompt: What is the speaker correcting?

competence.raw: M-I · 1.6 · corregir malentendidos + relativo + pasiva de regulación · listening
competence.topic: corregir malentendidos + relativo + pasiva de regulación

options.text: an outdated tariff that no longer applies

audio.transcript: — Please allow me to clear up that misunderstanding: the tariff, which appears in the old catalog, is strictly regulated and no longer applies.

items.prompt: How does the colleague frame the situation?

competence.raw: M-II · 2.1 · sentimientos en el trabajo + pros/contras · listening

options.text: by weighing pros and cons (on the one hand… on the other hand…)

audio.transcript: — Honestly, I feel overwhelmed by the split in the delegation. — I understand. On the one hand, the reform is risky; on the other hand, it could secure our future.

items.prompt: What advice is given?

competence.raw: M-II · 2.2 · consejo y órdenes asertivas + primer condicional · listening
competence.topic: consejo y órdenes asertivas + primer condicional

options.text: breathe, trust the preparation and focus on one face

audio.transcript: — I have terrible stage fright before the world panel. — Calm down and take a deep breath. You need to trust your preparation; if you feel nervous, focus on one friendly face.

parts.title: Part B — A briefing
parts.instructions: Read the text and answer the questions.

shared.title: Summit compliance briefing
shared.text: If our cooperative had not filed the complaint last month, the operator would have kept canceling our confirmed bookings. The account, which is now under compliance review, has been flagged, so no rebooking is possible until it is cleared. It is highly probable that the cancellation fees will be waived once the audit is complete. The delegation is likely to arrive at approximately nine forty; a revised schedule is being circulated. On the one hand the delay is frustrating; on the other hand, the review protects every member of the network.

items.prompt: Formal complaint / claim letter to an OTA (120-160 words). Write a formal complaint letter to an international OTA. The cooperative's account has been blocked and the operator has been cancelling confirmed bookings. Explain the problem (present perfect / present perfect continuous), demand concrete actions assertively (I am writing to request..., we require that...) and ask for the cancellation fees to be waived (might be waived).
items.source_rubric: formal and assertive register · present perfect (continuous) for the problem · clear and polite demands · correct technical terms (compliance / cancellation fees / waived) · cohesion, precision and spelling

items.prompt: Choose ONE: (a) Chair's meeting summary OR (b) 'Colombia, a Mediator's Perspective' (120-160 words). (a) the chair's summary of a negotiation: opens the session, summarises positions, records the disagreement (we strongly disagree) and closes on time; or (b) the climate defence 'Colombia, a Mediator's Perspective': integrate advanced conditionals (If we had not integrated..., ... would be...) and compound passive (has been protected, would be closed).

questions.text: Write your text here. Choose option (a) or option (b).

items.source_rubric: (a) meeting-minutes structure + chairing/negotiating language + closing; or (b) persuasive defence with advanced conditionals + compound passive + narration; cohesion and precision

parts.title: Speaking (written answer)
parts.instructions: Write your answer in English, as if you were speaking.

items.prompt: Chair a negotiation (mini-pitch). In the London executive room: open the meeting politely (I am pleased to open...), ask for a summary of reasons (Could you provide a summary...?), record a firm disagreement (we strongly disagree) and close on time. Then briefly defend the value of the destination with an advanced conditional.

questions.text: Write what you would say here.

items.source_rubric: chairs with the right formulas · handles disagreement firmly and tactfully · uses an advanced conditional in the defence · orderly closing · intelligibility

source_notes: b2-fa-l-11: source item 11 is the matching task; it counts as 5 items and is left out of the per-module map

b2-fa-w-01 and b2-fa-w-02: the source asks for 120-160 words. The platform keeps 1500 characters of each answer (the shared cap of 300 would cut a letter at about 45 words) and serves 120 and 160 as a hint; the rubric counts words in a wider window

b2-fa-w-02: the source makes Task 2 a choice of one of two prompts; the platform has no choice of task, so both prompts are shown in one item with one box, and the rubric credits the language of either one

Speaking Task 1 (b2-fa-s-01, read the Writing letter aloud) is NOT in this form: it has no written equivalent yet and needs a pedagogical decision. The Speaking section keeps its 15% weight and holds Task 2 only (0 to 5)
Speaking is delivered as a typed answer (delivery: written_equivalent); it does not measure pronunciation

The source has no figure briefs or alt text, so no item has an image and image_pending is not set anywhere; it also gives no instructions per part, so the part titles and instructions are ours (see REVIEW-B2-checkin.md)
spoken text: acronym spelled out for the voice: GDS -> G D S
